title: Getting started with brfssdata

title: Getting started with brfssdata

Labels available 1998 ; CDC longer distributes label files earlier years.

title: Survey-weighted logistic regression with BRFSS
text: brfss_design() returns srvyr design era-correct weight applied. Recodes work numeric codes, way epidemiologic BRFSS analyses ; brfss_labels() codebook documents code means.
code: library(brfssdata) library(dplyr) library(srvyr) library(survey)  des <- brfss_design(   2023,   vars = c("GENHLTH", "SEXVAR", "_AGE_G", "EDUCA"),   quiet = TRUE )  brfss_labels("EDUCA", years = 2023) #> # A tibble: 7 × 5 #>    year variable  code label                                            complete #>   <int> <chr>    <int> <chr>                                            <lgl>    #> 1  2023 EDUCA        2 Grades 1 through 8 (Elementary)                  TRUE     #> 2  2023 EDUCA        4 Grade 12 or GED (High school graduate)           TRUE     #> 3  2023 EDUCA        1 Never attended school or only kindergarten       TRUE     #> 4  2023 EDUCA        3 Grades 9 through 11 (Some high school)           TRUE     #> 5  2023 EDUCA        6 College 4 years or more (College graduate)       TRUE     #> 6  2023 EDUCA        5 College 1 year to 3 years (Some college or tech… TRUE     #> 7  2023 EDUCA        9 Refused                                          TRUE

title: Survey-weighted logistic regression with BRFSS
text: outcome fair poor self-rated health (codes 4 5); don’t-know (7) refused (9) become missing. Education collapses three levels. Everything ordinary dplyr design object; srvyr keeps design attached.
code: des <- des |>   mutate(     fairpoor = case_when(       GENHLTH %in% 4:5 ~ 1,       GENHLTH %in% 1:3 ~ 0,       .default = NA     ),     sex = factor(SEXVAR, 1:2, c("Male", "Female")),     edu3 = case_when(       EDUCA %in% 1:3 ~ "Less than high school",       EDUCA %in% 4:5 ~ "High school or some college",       EDUCA == 6 ~ "College graduate",       .default = NA     ) |> factor(levels = c(       "College graduate",       "High school or some college",       "Less than high school"     )),     age_g = factor(`_AGE_G`, 1:6, c(       "18-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65+"     ))   )

title: Survey-weighted logistic regression with BRFSS
code: des |>   filter(!is.na(fairpoor)) |>   group_by(edu3) |>   summarize(prev = survey_mean(fairpoor, vartype = "ci")) |>   na.omit() #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   edu3                          prev prev_low prev_upp #>   <fct>                        <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 College graduate            0.0974   0.0945    0.100 #> 2 High school or some college 0.203    0.199     0.207 #> 3 Less than high school       0.406    0.394     0.418

title: Survey-weighted logistic regression with BRFSS
text: svyglm() accepts design object directly. quasibinomial family standard choice survey weights. education gradient headline: relative college graduates, odds fair poor health substantially higher lower education levels, net sex age, pattern consistent across BRFSS years one reason self-rated health workhorse outcome health disparities research.
code: fit <- svyglm(   fairpoor ~ sex + age_g + edu3,   design = des,   family = quasibinomial() )  # Odds ratios with design-based confidence intervals or <- exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit), confint(fit))) round(or[-1, ], 2) #>                                   OR 2.5 % 97.5 % #> sexFemale                       1.11  1.07   1.15 #> age_g25-34                      1.37  1.25   1.50 #> age_g35-44                      1.59  1.46   1.74 #> age_g45-54                      2.11  1.94   2.30 #> age_g55-64                      2.72  2.50   2.95 #> age_g65+                        2.82  2.61   3.04 #> edu3High school or some college 2.50  2.40   2.60 #> edu3Less than high school       6.78  6.38   7.21

title: Survey-weighted logistic regression with BRFSS
text: Multi-year designs pool brfss_design(2019:2023); weights averaged across years strata become year--stratum interactions. Requests spanning 2011 fail purpose; see getting-started vignette redesign details. brfss_labels("EDUCA") documents every code, including special values (9 Refused ) usually become NA. what: Access CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System Data
title: Access CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System Data
text: brfssdata gives R users direct, reproducible access annual microdata CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), largest continuously conducted health telephone survey world. Survey years processed compact parquet files hosted GitHub release assets. package downloads requested year single time local cache, queries DuckDB (pulling handful variables 300-plus column survey fast), hands back either tibble ready-made srvyr survey-design object correct weights, strata, primary sampling units survey era. Status: 40 available survey years (1985-2024) published data releases; 1984 never distributed SAS Transport file CDC. brfss_years() always reports currently hosted years.

title: Access CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System Data
text: Downloads cached brfss_cache_dir() (per tools::R_user_dir()), everything first pull works offline. brfss_cache_info() brfss_cache_clear() manage cache.
code: library(brfssdata)  # Which survey years are published? brfss_years()  # Respondent-level data, only the variables you need dat <- read_brfss(2019:2023, vars = c("GENHLTH", "PHYSHLTH", "_LLCPWT"))  # The same, with safe categoricals converted to labeled factors dat <- read_brfss(2023, vars = c("GENHLTH", "SEXVAR"), labels = TRUE)  # The value-label codebook itself (1998 onward) brfss_labels("GENHLTH", years = 2023)  # A survey-design object with era-correct weights, ready for srvyr library(srvyr) brfss_design(2023, vars = "GENHLTH") |>   group_by(GENHLTH) |>   summarize(prop = survey_prop(vartype = "ci"))  # Where does a variable appear across years? brfss_vars("smok")

what: Build a survey-design object for BRFSS analysis — brfss_design
title: Build a survey-design object for BRFSS analysis — brfss_design
text: Returns srvyr::as_survey_design() tbl_svy complex sampling design applied: primary sampling units (_PSU), strata (_STSTR), year-appropriate final weight. Weight selection automatic: _FINALWT years 2011 (post-stratification era) _LLCPWT 2011 (raking era). CDC states estimates 2011 onward directly comparable earlier years, 2011 added cell-phone-respondents replaced post-stratification raking. Requests pool years sides boundary therefore fail unless allow_break = TRUE set deliberately. several years combined, weights divided number years (pool_weights = TRUE, default) pooled estimates represent average year rather sum populations, variance strata become year--stratum interaction, treating annual survey independent sample. BRFSS public-use files make respondent primary sampling unit, single-PSU strata common make variance estimation fail. options(survey.lonely.psu) unset, function sets "adjust" (standard BRFSS practice) says per session; option set always respected.

title: Build a survey-design object for BRFSS analysis — brfss_design
code: brfss_design(   years,   vars = NULL,   allow_break = FALSE,   pool_weights = TRUE,   download = TRUE,   quiet = FALSE,   labels = FALSE )

title: Build a survey-design object for BRFSS analysis — brfss_design
text: years Integer vector survey years, e.g. 2023 2019:2023. See brfss_years() available. vars Optional character vector analysis variables carry design. Design variables always included. allow_break Set TRUE permit pooling years across 2011 methodology change. warning still issued. pool_weights TRUE one year requested, divide weight number years. download FALSE, cached years used missing years raise error instead downloaded. quiet TRUE, suppress download progress output. labels TRUE, convert variables safe value-label maps factors using CDC's format libraries (available 1998 ). variable converts format pure code--label map, code set agrees across requested years, every observed value covered; everything else keeps numeric codes. See brfss_labels() raw catalog.

title: Build a survey-design object for BRFSS analysis — brfss_design
text: tbl_svy survey-design object. underlying data carry three added syntactic columns design built : brfss_wt (selected, possibly pooled, weight), brfss_psu, brfss_strata (raw stratum single year; year--stratum interaction years pooled). original CDC columns kept unchanged.

what: brfssdata: Access CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System Data — brfssdata-package
title: brfssdata: Access CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System Data — brfssdata-package
text: Download, cache, analyze annual microdata United States Centers Disease Control Prevention Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/. Survey years stored compact files hosted public releases queried lazily 'DuckDB' (via 'duckdb' package), requested years variables transferred. Survey-design helpers construct 'srvyr' design objects year-appropriate weights, strata, primary sampling units, including explicit handling 2011 weighting methodology change.

title: Read BRFSS survey microdata — read_brfss
text: Returns respondent-level BRFSS data one survey years tibble. requested year downloaded local cache (see brfss_cache_dir()) read afterwards; query runs DuckDB, selecting handful variables 300-plus column survey stays fast. Different survey years carry different variable sets. years combined, variables absent year filled NA. year column always identifies survey year row.

Use brfss_vars() search names across years. download FALSE, cached years used missing years raise error instead downloaded. quiet TRUE, suppress download progress output. labels TRUE, convert variables safe value-label maps factors using CDC's format libraries (available 1998 ). variable converts format pure code--label map, code set agrees across requested years, every observed value covered; everything else keeps numeric codes. See brfss_labels() raw catalog.
